free_tier.stated: Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address, gaining access to free hands-on labs to learn and practice cloud skills in real-time.

egress.terms: no credit and no transfer allowance is stated on the page; the offer is lab access; ingress: none
egress.free_allowance: no credit and no transfer allowance is stated on the page; the offer is lab access

tooling: nothing to run: no instance is issued
chaining: no chain; it is a training programme rather than a source of capacity

limits.value: access is to curated lab sessions rather than to an account a user controls

binding_note: there is no volume to run out of: a user never gets an instance or a public address, so 1 TiB a month is not reachable at any price through this programme.

identity_cost.detail: No credit card needed. Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address.

reliability_note: lab sessions are time-boxed and reset, so nothing installed survives
confidence_note: the page's absence of a credit line is what is being reported

evidence.proved: 'Learners as young as 13 can register for AWS Educate with just an email address, gaining access to free hands-on labs', 'No credit card needed', and 'AWS Educate offers an extensive library of free, self-paced online training'

notes: The only programme with no card and no institution, and it buys no capacity: the page describes training and labs, names no credit and no instance. Read as an absence rather than a number, which is why it is recorded at all: a reader who sees 'no credit card needed' will otherwise spend the session finding out.

extras.wg_detail: the programme grants lab sessions rather than an account with a public IPv4, so there is no endpoint for wg-quick to bind
extras.volume_stated: no credit and no transfer allowance is stated on the page; the offer is lab access
extras.transit_note: the bytes stay inside AWS's lab environment and never reach a client-controlled endpoint
